```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A shows clearer evidence that people will pay. One sourced demand quote says the founder already pays a human bookkeeper ('It costs a lot'). Several competitors publish paid tiers at $29-100/mo, and human-led Bench charges $250-699/mo. B's core feature is given away free by Kintsugi, Numeral and TaxJar, which leaves little room for a $29-49/mo standalone price.",
    "B faces a substitute that removes the need for the product. Its own sourced evidence says indie founders solve the problem by moving to a Merchant of Record such as Paddle or Lemon Squeezy, which takes on the tax liability. A's free-tier competitors still leave a paid upgrade path. B's free monitors exist to funnel users into filing, which B does not offer.",
    "A's demand evidence is broader and more current: three independent, linked quotes, including a quantified 3-4 hours per month of reconciliation pain. B has two quotes, and one dates from 2020.",
    "A has a distribution channel that is both specific and low-cost: the Stripe App Marketplace, which is sourced and reaches Stripe users directly. B's sourced newsletter CPC of $0.52 is encouraging, but its SEO channel runs into heavy existing content from funded competitors.",
    "A's brief names a buildable narrower wedge (pure Stripe-to-bank reconciliation) that fits mechanical, agent-driven automation. B's open questions suggest the real need may be a decision tool, not the monitor as described."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B rests its feasibility and differentiation case on Tax Threshold Radar, a 'nearly identical solo-built product' at $49/mo. The brief itself admits the testimonials could not be verified and that it may be an unvalidated landing page. That means there is no evidence anyone pays for monitoring-only.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both ideas face crowded markets with free alternatives. A has serious unresolved problems. Its trust and SOC2 expectations are hard for a solo operator to meet. Kick's free tier may already cover the low-volume segment. The Growthy figure of $400-600/mo in bookkeeper time has no link, so it counts as missing. Data-privacy requirements are marked [unsourced]. Neither brief shows verified revenue for a lean comparable. A wins mainly because B's free-competitor and Merchant of Record problems directly undercut its willingness to pay."
}
```
